title: Post-Quantum Cryptography Initiative
description:
# Post-Quantum Cryptography Initiative
## CISA Approach
- **Provide Technical Guidance and Risk Management Strategies for PQC Implementation (** [**Executive Order [EO] 14412**](https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2026/06/securing-the-nation-against-advanced-cryptographic-attacks/) **)**: CISA consults with NIST and the National Security Agency (NSA) to provide federal departments and agencies with technical guidance on PQC implementation, including best practices and risk management strategies. Additionally, CISA works with Sector Risk Management Agencies (SRMA) to assist critical infrastructure owners and operators in developing PQC migration planning.
- [**Product Category Identification**](https://www.cisa.gov/resources-tools/resources/product-categories-technologies-use-post-quantum-cryptography-standards)**(** [**EO 14306**](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2025/06/11/2025-10804/sustaining-select-efforts-to-strengthen-the-nations-cybersecurity-and-amending-executive-order-13694)**)**: CISA develops and regularly updates a list of product categories that include technologies that support or plan to support PQC standard algorithms.

## PQC Related Resources
### NIST Guidance
- [**PQC Federal Information Processing Standards (FIPS)**](https://csrc.nist.gov/news/2024/postquantum-cryptography-fips-approved) **.** On August 13, 2024, NIST approved three PQC standards—FIPS 203, FIPS 204, and FIPS 205—to help protect federal systems from future quantum computing threats.
- [**Post-Quantum Cryptography Project**](https://csrc.nist.gov/projects/post-quantum-cryptography) **.** The NIST PQC Project leads the effort to evaluate and standardize cryptographic algorithms that can withstand quantum computing threats.
- [**Cryptographic Module Validation Program**](https://csrc.nist.gov/projects/cryptographic-module-validation-program) **.** This joint effort between NIST and Canada’s Centre for Cyber Security certifies encryption modules that meet FIPS 140-2 and FIPS 140-3 standards. It supports ongoing FIPS 140-3 validations and provides a transition plan for older FIPS 140-2 modules through 2026.
- [**Cryptographic Algorithm Validation Program**](https://csrc.nist.gov/projects/cryptographic-algorithm-validation-program) **.** This program uses automated testing to check whether vendors’ FIPS-approved cryptographic algorithms work correctly before they can be certified by National Voluntary Laboratory Accreditation Program-accredited labs and listed as validated.

### GSA Guidance
- [**PQC Buyers Guide**](https://buy.gsa.gov/api/system/files/documents/final-508c-pqc_buyer-s_guide_2025.pdf) **.** GSA designed this guide to enable agencies to safeguard existing systems from both classical and quantum computer-based risks and maintain the confidentiality and integrity of data communications.

### DHS Guidance
- [**DHS PQC Roadmap**](https://www.dhs.gov/quantum) **.** This roadmap, jointly produced by DHS and NIST, outlines the risks posed by advances in quantum computing and guides organizations in preparing for the transition to PQC through inventory, planning, and risk-based modernization of cryptographic systems.

### NSA Guidance
- [**CNSA 2.0 and Quantum Computing FAQ**](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Sep/07/2003071836/-1/-1/1/CSI_CNSA_2.0_FAQ_.PDF). This document clarifies Commercial National Security Algorithm Suite 2.0 (CNSA 2.0) requirements for National Security Systems (NSS) and recommended guidance for the Department of War (DoW) and the Defense Industrial Base (DIB).
- [**NSA Post-Quantum Cybersecurity Resources**](https://www.nsa.gov/Cybersecurity/Post-Quantum-Cybersecurity-Resources/). This resources page outlines NSA’s guidance on quantum-resistant cryptography, naming approved algorithms under Committee on National Security Systems Policy 15 and advising caution with quantum key distribution until current technical limits are resolved.

description:
# EU post-quantum cryptography roadmap: is a timeline alone sufficient?
The EU has set quantum-safe cryptography transition deadlines: deployment starts in 2026, concluding by 2030 for critical use cases, and by 2035 for all remaining systems.

## Companies preparing ahead for the quantum-challenge
- **By the end of 2030:** High-risk use cases (e.g. financial, health) or critical infrastructures (e.g. energy, telecommunications) must be transitioned to quantum-safe (PQC) algorithms.

## A trusted technological partner in quantum and quantum-safe technologies
The company is already making strides towards quantum-safe networks by integrating an additional layer of protection through quantum-resistant technologies.

In this context, [Telefónica’s Quantum-Safe Networks offer communication and cybersecurity solutions](https://www.telefonicaempresas.es/grandes-empresas/tecnologias/redes-quantum-safe/) designed to protect companies’ critical communications and data against the threats posed by quantum computing.
